newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas mostly up on weather, stock refills.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas mostly up on weather, stock refills.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were mostly higher Monday due to continued storage buying and warmer weather in the Northeast and upper Midwest, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices rose an average of two cents to about $2.15-2.20 per mmBtu, with Henry Hub quoted at $2.17-2.20.
Similarly in south Texas prices gained about one cent to $2.09-2.12. Temperatures in Houston were expected to reach highs near 90 degrees F throughout this week, according to Weather Services Corp.
In west Texas, Permian prices climbed about one cent higher to about $1.97-1.99, while Waha values were quoted again at $2.05-2.07.
Southern California prices rose five cents to about $2.14-2.15 despite temperature highs only in the high-70s in Los Angeles.
Traders speculated that West Coast buyers entered the market for storage gas.
In the Midwest, prices eased by about one cent to about $2.03-2.04, with Chicago city-gate quoted in the low-to-mid $2.20s.
At the Detroit city-gate, gas sold at $2.28-2.33, down about two cents from Friday's levels.
In the East, New York city gate prices gained at least five cents to about $2.45-2.50 as temperatures in the region were expected to reach about 90 degrees F on Wednesday, according to WSC.
